well: ICDP borehole 5017-1 - DEAD SEA BASIN, deep northern basin center (31.508 N, 35.471 E), drilled from a barge through 300 m of hypersaline water (per the file's own event comment); the lake surface sits at ~-428 m elevation (per the companion DSDDP dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.944827) making this the LOWEST drilling site on Earth and the catalogue's first LAKE borehole - 457 m of sediment recovered spanning 220 kyr on the Dead Sea Transform plate boundary; this dataset scans the debrite at 172.055-172.130 m
operator_on_log: Lu, Pope, Moernaut, Bookman, Waldmann, Agnon, Marco & Strasser (Innsbruck/Durham/Haifa/HUJI/TAU) - XRF core-scanner element counts (Ca, Ti) and magnetic susceptibility at 1-mm resolution through a single mass-flow deposit (debrite); ICDP Dead Sea Deep Drilling Project (DSDDP), 2010-2011; FWF grant M 2817 ('a 220 kyr-long continuous earthquake record')
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.938390 ('Ca, Ti, MS of ICDP core 5017-1, Debrite (Fig. 2u)'), in bundle doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.938454; supplement to Lu et al. 2022, EPSL 594, 117723 (doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2022.117723); Curation Level: Enhanced curation
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0), declared IN the file's own header. Attribution: Lu et al. / PANGAEA / ICDP / FWF M 2817
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (228 data points per the header's own Size declaration = 76 rows x 3 parameters with depth as geocode, EXACT) in one fetch. DISCLOSURE: two larger Dead Sea candidates were examined first and left OUT under the complete-dataset rule - the seismogenic mass-failure inventory (doi 931843) is an XLSX binary outside the verbatim-textfile route, and the annually-resolved varve table (doi 944827, 2,648 points) is too large to transcribe verbatim with confidence through this environment
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 76 measurements at UNIFORM 1-mm spacing, 172.055-172.130 m sediment depth - Ca 6,346-20,120 cps, Ti 16-225 cps, magnetic susceptibility -9 to +25 x10^-6 SI - a full anatomical scan of one earthquake-related sediment-density-flow deposit in the hypersaline lake record
curves: Depth sed [m] 172.055-172.130 (GEOCODE; all 75 steps exactly 0.001 m - the catalogue's finest depth resolution)
Ca [cps] (XRF core scanner; authigenic aragonite proxy)
MAGS [10^-6 SI] (magnetic susceptibility; NEGATIVE = diamagnetic evaporite matrix)
source_anomaly_disclosure: No internal inconsistencies detected - the archive's numbers close cleanly; noted for the record: this dataset is the archive's own figure-support excerpt (its title carries 'Fig. 2u'), a complete dataset in its own right with its own DOI and Size declaration, scoped by the source to one debrite; MS values are stored at integer resolution with three trailing zeros
purpose: thirty-eighth catalogue entry - the DEAD SEA BASIN joins as region TWENTY-SIX (the catalogue's first lake borehole, first on-land-below-sea-level site, first hypersaline system, and first plate-boundary transform record - drilled for PALEOSEISMOLOGY: a 220-kyr earthquake archive, the natural-hazard companion to the catalogue's laboratory friction and slow-slip entries) and XRF core scanning + MS profiling is kind TWENTY-SEVEN at the catalogue's finest resolution (1 mm); the debrite's anatomy is re-derived by the gate on every run: a DIAMAGNETIC evaporite matrix (33 of 76 rows below zero, floor -9e-6 SI - aragonite and halite repelling the field), ONE positive detrital excursion (peak +25) whose MS >= 10 band carries 1.99x the mean Ti of the diamagnetic intervals (detrital magnetite and clay riding in the flow), and the aragonite cap at the very top of the scan holding the highest Ca count (20,120 cps)
verified: 76 rows / 228 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (EXACT); uniform 1-mm grid on all 75 increments; MS range [-9, +25] with 33 diamagnetic rows; detrital coupling pinned (mean Ti in the MS>=10 band / mean Ti in the MS<=0 band = 1.99); Ca maximum at the first row; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
